title: Container Bookings: Rejected Dangerous-Goods Containers in Goodwill Decisions
content:
When the line has rejected a dangerous-goods acceptance on a Container Bookings booking, the containers under that acceptance affect whether the booking's changes are treated as owing fees when goodwill on a customer roll fee is considered.

## Rule

For this purpose the booking's chargeable containers are what is left of its container quantity once the containers named on the rejected acceptance are set aside, the figure never going below zero; if no acceptance has been rejected, the whole quantity is chargeable. Where the chargeable containers come to zero, a destination change or customer roll on the booking owes no fee and so does not leave the change account incomplete.

Should the line have rejected two or more dangerous-goods acceptances on the same booking, these goodwill rules do not reach it, since they give no chargeable-container figure for that case.

## Where the facts come from

The container quantity is read from the booking record; the status and container count of each acceptance come from the dangerous-goods acceptance records linked to the booking.

## Hypothetical cases

| Booking quantity | Rejected acceptance | Chargeable containers | Effect on completeness |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | none | 5 | changes are assessed normally |
| 5 | covering 2 | 3 | changes are assessed normally |
| 5 | covering 5 | 0 | the booking's changes owe no fee |
| 5 | two acceptances rejected | undefined | outside these rules |

Quantities are illustrative.
